theme.title: The Lord Is Risen
theme.summary: From the empty tomb to the upper room and the fire of Pentecost: fifty days of Easter, one step each day, until the Spirit sends the Church out.

topics.name: Easter
topics.summary: The season as a whole: the Resurrection, the risen body, the Lord's Day, the Eucharist and the sacraments of initiation, the Ascension, Pentecost and the witnesses.

levels.title: The Lord's Day and the Easter Feast
Baptism and the Sacraments of Initiation

topics.name: Easter Challenge
topics.summary: One day of Easter at a time, from Easter Sunday to Pentecost.

levels.title: He Is Not Here
levels.reflection: On the first day of the week the women come to the tomb with spices and find the stone rolled back and the body gone. Two men in shining garments ask the question the whole Church repeats at Easter: why seek you the living with the dead? He is not here, but is risen. Peter runs in and sees the linen cloths lying, and the other disciple goes in, sees, and believes. The Catechism calls the empty tomb an essential sign, though not itself a proof, and calls the Resurrection the crowning truth of our faith in Christ. Everything we have kept in Lent leads to this morning. Christ is risen.

scripture.text: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their countenance towards the ground, they said unto them: Why seek you the living with the dead? He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spoke unto you, when he was in Galilee,

saint.name: St. Jerome
saint.reference: Easter homily, as quoted in CCC 1166
saint.text: The Lord's day, the day of Resurrection, the day of Christians, is our day. It is called the Lord's day because on it the Lord rose victorious to the Father. If pagans call it the "day of the sun," we willingly agree, for today the light of the world is raised.

levels.title: Fear Not
levels.reflection: The women leave the tomb quickly, with fear and great joy, running to tell his disciples, and on the road Jesus himself meets them. His first word is a greeting: All hail. They take hold of his feet and adore him. Then he says what he has said throughout the Gospel to those who are afraid: fear not. Go, tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, there they shall see me. The Catechism says that the women were the first to encounter the Risen One and the first messengers of Christ's Resurrection to the apostles themselves. Easter begins with people who were told to go and tell.

scripture.text: And behold Jesus met them, saying: All hail. But they came up and took hold of his feet, and adored him. Then Jesus said to them: Fear not. Go, tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, there they shall see me.

saint.name: St. Hippolytus
saint.reference: On the Pasch 1-2, as quoted in CCC 1165
saint.text: Life extends over all beings and fills them with unlimited light; the Orient of orients pervades the universe, and he who was "before the daystar" and before the heavenly bodies, immortal and vast, the great Christ, shines over all beings more brightly than.

levels.title: He Called Her by Name
levels.reflection: Mary Magdalene stands weeping outside the tomb. She turns and sees a man whom she takes for the gardener, and asks him where the body has been laid. Jesus says only one word: Mary. She turns and says, Rabboni, which is to say, Master. He sends her to his brethren with the great message: I ascend to my Father and to your Father, to my God and your God. She goes and tells the disciples that she has seen the Lord. The risen Christ does not first prove himself. He calls us by name, and then he sends us. That is how Easter faith usually begins.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master).

levels.title: Did Not Our Heart Burn
levels.reflection: Two disciples are walking away from Jerusalem when Jesus himself draws near and goes with them, but their eyes are held that they should not know him. He opens the Scriptures, and when he sits at table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them. Their eyes are opened and he vanishes. Was not our heart burning within us, they say, whilst he spoke in this way, and opened to us the scriptures? At once they return to Jerusalem and tell how they knew him in the breaking of the bread. The Catechism notes that this is how the disciples recognized him after the Resurrection, and why the first Christians called the Eucharist the breaking of bread.

scripture.text: And it came to pass, whilst he was at table with them, he took bread, and blessed, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him: and he vanished out of their sight. And they said one to the other: Was not our heart burning within us, whilst he spoke in this way, and opened to us the scriptures?

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: On the Sacraments 5, 4, 26, as quoted in CCC 2836
saint.text: If you receive the bread each day, each day is today for you. If Christ is yours today, he rises for you every day. How can this be? "You are my Son, today I have begotten you." Therefore, "today" is when Christ rises.

levels.title: Peace Be to You
levels.reflection: While the two from Emmaus are still speaking, Jesus stands in the midst of the disciples and says: Peace be to you; it is I, fear not. They are frightened and think they see a spirit, so he shows them his hands and his feet. Handle, and see, he says, for a spirit hath not flesh and bones. When they still wonder for joy, he asks if they have anything to eat, and takes a piece of broiled fish before them. The Catechism teaches that by touch and the sharing of a meal the risen Jesus shows he is not a ghost, and that the body is the same body that was crucified, now with new properties. The Resurrection is real.

scripture.text: Now whilst they were speaking these things, Jesus stood in the midst of them, and saith to them: Peace be to you; it is I, fear not. But they being troubled and frightened, supposed that they saw a spirit. And he said to them: Why are you troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? See my hands and feet, that it is I myself; handle, and see: for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as you see me to have.

saint.name: St. Irenaeus
saint.reference: Against Heresies 4, 18, 4-5, as quoted in CCC 1000
saint.text: so too our bodies, which partake of the Eucharist, are no longer corruptible, but possess the hope of resurrection.

levels.title: It Is the Lord
levels.reflection: Seven of the disciples have fished all night and caught nothing when a figure on the shore tells them to cast the net on the right side of the ship. The net is so full they cannot draw it in. The disciple whom Jesus loved says to Peter: it is the Lord. Peter girds his coat about him and throws himself into the sea. On the shore a fire of coals is laid and fish and bread are ready, and Jesus says: come, and dine. None of them dare to ask who he is, for they know. Peter will say before the council that there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved. The Catechism says the name Jesus means God saves.

scripture.text: He saith to them: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and you shall find. They cast therefore; and now they were not able to draw it, for the multitude of fishes. That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved, said to Peter: It is the Lord. Simon Peter, when he heard that it was the Lord, girt his coat about him, (for he was naked,) and cast himself into the sea.

saint.name: St. Peter Chrysologus
saint.reference: Sermon 71, 4, as quoted in CCC 2814
saint.text: We ask God to hallow his name, which by its own holiness saves and makes holy all creation .... It is this name that gives salvation to a lost world.

levels.title: We Cannot But Speak
levels.reflection: Peter and John have been brought before the council and told to speak no more in the name of Jesus. They answer with a question: if it be just in the sight of God to hear you rather than God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. The risen Lord had told his disciples to go into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature. The Catechism teaches that the witness of a Christian life and good works done in a supernatural spirit have great power to draw men to the faith and to God. The Easter message is first told, and then lived.

scripture.text: But Peter and John answering, said to them: If it be just in the sight of God, to hear you rather than God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

levels.title: My Lord and My God
levels.reflection: A week after Easter the disciples are together again, and Thomas is with them. He had said that unless he put his finger into the nails and his hand into the side, he would not believe. Jesus comes, the doors being shut, and tells Thomas to put in his finger and see, and to be not faithless, but believing. Thomas answers with the plainest confession in the Gospels: my Lord, and my God. Jesus blesses those who have not seen and have believed. The Church keeps this Sunday as the second Sunday of Easter, which the U.S. calendar also calls the Sunday of Divine Mercy, because here the wounds of Christ become the door to mercy.

scripture.text: Then he saith to Thomas: Put in thy finger hither, and see my hands; and bring hither thy hand, and put it into my side; and be not faithless, but believing. Thomas answered, and said to him: My Lord, and my God. Jesus saith to him: Because thou hast seen me, Thomas, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed.

saint.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
saint.reference: Adoro te devote, as quoted in CCC 1381
saint.text: Seeing, touching, tasting are in thee deceived; How says trusty hearing? that shall be believed; What God's Son has told me, take for truth I do; Truth himself speaks truly or there's nothing true.

levels.title: Born from Above
levels.reflection: Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, comes to Jesus by night. Jesus tells him something that cannot be learned from books: unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. The Spirit breathes where he will; you hear his voice but know not whence he comes or whither he goes. In the Easter season the Church hears this above all as the language of Baptism. The Catechism calls it the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit, for it signifies and actually brings about the birth of water and the Spirit. We are not only taught new things. We are made new.

scripture.text: Jesus answered: Amen, amen I say to thee, unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

saint.name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
saint.reference: Commentary on Matthew 2, 5, as quoted in CCC 537
saint.text: Everything that happened to Christ lets us know that, after the bath of water, the Holy Spirit swoops down upon us from high heaven and that, adopted by the Father's voice, we become sons of God.

levels.title: One Heart and One Soul
levels.reflection: The first Christians in Jerusalem did not form a committee. The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul, and no one called anything his own, but all things were common to them. Luke says they sold their possessions and goods and divided them to all, according as every one had need. They persevered in the teaching of the apostles, the breaking of bread, and prayer. The Catechism sees in that sequence the shape of the Church's prayer: founded on the apostolic faith, authenticated by charity, nourished in the Eucharist. Easter is not only something we believe about Jesus. It is a way of living together.

scripture.text: And the multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul: neither did any one say that aught of the things which he possessed, was his own; but all things were common unto them.

saint.name: Origen
saint.reference: Homilies on Ezekiel 9, 1, as quoted in CCC 817
saint.text: Where there are sins, there are also divisions, schisms, heresies, and disputes. Where there is virtue, however, there also are harmony and unity, from which arise the one heart and one soul of all believers.

levels.title: God So Loved the World
levels.reflection: In the same night talk with Nicodemus, Jesus says the line the Church has treasured above many others: God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him may not perish, but may have life everlasting. He adds that God sent not his Son into the world to judge it, but that the world may be saved by him. The Catechism teaches that the Word became flesh so that we might know God's love. In Easter that love is no longer an idea. It has a wounded, risen body, and it has not stopped.

scripture.text: For God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son; that whosoever believeth in him, may not perish, but may have life everlasting.

saint.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
saint.reference: Catechetical Lectures 18, 29, as quoted in CCC 1050
saint.text: True and subsistent life consists in this: the Father, through the Son and in the Holy Spirit, pouring out his heavenly gifts on all things without exception. Thanks to his mercy, we too, men that we are, have received the inalienable promise of eternal life.

levels.title: We Ought to Obey God
levels.reflection: The apostles have been jailed and set free by an angel, and then brought before the council again and told to stop teaching in the name of Jesus. Peter and the apostles answer plainly: we ought to obey God, rather than men. It is the answer of people who have met the risen Lord. John gives the reason a few lines earlier: he that believeth in the Son hath life everlasting. The Catechism says a citizen is obliged in conscience not to follow civil directives contrary to the moral order, the rights of persons or the Gospel, and quotes these very words. Easter faith makes people free and brave.

scripture.text: But Peter and the apostles answering, said: We ought to obey God, rather than men.

levels.title: Five Loaves and Two Fishes
levels.reflection: A great crowd follows Jesus up the mountain, and he asks Philip where bread can be bought for them all. A boy has five barley loaves and two fishes, but what are these among so many? Jesus takes the loaves, gives thanks, and distributes them as much as they would. When all are filled, he tells his disciples to gather up the fragments that remain, lest they be lost. Twelve baskets are filled. In the same season Gamaliel warns the council about the apostles: if this work be of God, you cannot overthrow it. The Church has always heard the multiplication as a sign of the Eucharist.

scripture.text: And Jesus took the loaves: and when he had given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down. In like manner also of the fishes, as much as they would.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Sermon 57, 7, as quoted in CCC 2837
saint.text: The Eucharist is our daily bread. the power belonging to this divine food makes it a bond of union.

levels.title: It Is I; Be Not Afraid
levels.reflection: The disciples row across the lake in the dark, and when they have gone about five and twenty or thirty furlongs they see Jesus walking upon the sea, drawing nigh to the ship, and they are afraid. He says to them: it is I; be not afraid. They are glad to take him into the ship, and presently the ship is at the land where they were going. The same hour finds the apostles in Jerusalem, where the number of disciples is growing and the Twelve ask the community to look out seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. The risen Lord's word is the same at sea and in the Church: be not afraid.

scripture.text: When they had rowed therefore about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking upon the sea, and drawing nigh to the ship, and they were afraid. But he saith to them: It is I; be not afraid.

levels.title: He Opened Their Understanding
levels.reflection: On Easter evening Jesus tells the disciples that everything written about him in the law of Moses, in the prophets, and in the psalms must be fulfilled. Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures. He explains that it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise again from the dead the third day, and that penance and remission of sins should be preached in his name unto all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. You are witnesses of these things, he says. The Catechism teaches that through all the words of Scripture, God speaks only one single Word. The risen Lord is the key that opens the whole book.

scripture.text: And he said to them: These are the words which I spoke to you, while I was yet with you, that all things must needs be fulfilled, which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Commentary on Psalm 103, 4, 1, as quoted in CCC 102
saint.text: You recall that one and the same Word of God extends throughout Scripture, that it is one and the same Utterance that resounds in the mouths of all the sacred writers, since he who was in the beginning God with God has no need of separate syllables; for he is not subject to time.

levels.title: The Work of God
levels.reflection: The crowd that was fed on the hillside follows Jesus across the lake and asks: what shall we do, that we may work the works of God? He answers with a single work. This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he hath sent. Easter begins with faith, not with effort. In Jerusalem Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, is already doing great wonders and signs among the people, and when he stands before the council, those who look on him see his face as if it had been the face of an angel. The works that follow are the fruit of the faith, and they are possible because the risen Christ is at work in them.

scripture.text: They said therefore unto him: What shall we do, that we may work the works of God? Jesus answered, and said to them: This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he hath sent.

levels.title: Bread of Life
levels.reflection: I am the bread of life, says Jesus to the crowd at Capernaum: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth in me shall never thirst. The words were hard to hear then, and the Church has never softened them. In the same chapter of Acts Stephen stands before the council and, full of the Holy Spirit, sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God. As the stones fall he prays as Jesus did on the cross: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit, and Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. Then he fell asleep in the Lord. The Bread of life is also the strength of martyrs.

scripture.text: And Jesus said to them: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger: and he that believeth in me shall never thirst.

levels.title: I Will Not Cast Out
levels.reflection: All that the Father giveth to me shall come to me, says Jesus, and him that cometh to me I will not cast out. It is one of the gentlest sentences in the Gospel, and it sits beside a sober one: the will of the Father is that of all that he hath given me I should lose nothing, but raise it up again in the last day. The Church has always taken it as the promise behind the resurrection of the body. In Jerusalem, a persecution scatters the Christians, and they that were dispersed went about preaching the word of God. Every scattering of the Church has been an opportunity to carry the Gospel further.

scripture.text: All that the Father giveth to me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me, I will not cast out.

levels.title: Water on the Road
levels.reflection: An Ethiopian official, a eunuch in charge of the queen's treasure, rides home from Jerusalem reading the prophet Isaiah. Philip runs alongside and asks if he understands what he is reading. How can I, unless some man shew me, he says, and asks him to sit up beside him. Beginning at that Scripture Philip preaches to him Jesus. When they come to a certain water, the eunuch says: see, here is water: what doth hinder me from being baptized? Philip says that if he believes with all his heart, he may, and the man answers: I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. The Church still follows this pattern: preach Jesus, then baptize.

scripture.text: Then Philip, opening his mouth, and beginning at this scripture, preached unto him Jesus.

saint.name: St. Justin Martyr
saint.reference: First Apology 66, 1-2, as quoted in CCC 1355
saint.text: we call this food Eucharist, and no one may take part in it unless he believes that what we teach is true, has received baptism for the forgiveness of sins and new birth, and lives in keeping with what Christ taught.

levels.title: My Flesh Is Meat Indeed
levels.reflection: Jesus tells the crowd that he who eats his flesh and drinks his blood has everlasting life, and he will raise him up in the last day, for his flesh is meat indeed and his blood is drink indeed. The Church has never read this as a figure of speech. The Catechism says that in the Eucharist the body and blood, together with the soul and divinity, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and therefore the whole Christ, is truly, really and substantially contained. On the road to Damascus the risen Christ also asks Saul why he is persecuting him, so closely is his Body united with himself. Easter gives us a risen Christ who feeds us, and whom we may not hurt without hurting him.

scripture.text: He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath everlasting life: and I will raise him up in the last day. For my flesh is meat indeed: and my blood is drink indeed.

saint.name: St. John Chrysostom
saint.reference: On the Betrayal of Judas 1, 6, as quoted in CCC 1375
saint.text: It is not man that causes the things offered to become the Body and Blood of Christ, but he who was crucified for us, Christ himself. the priest, in the role of Christ, pronounces these words, but their power and grace are God's.

levels.title: To Whom Shall We Go?
levels.reflection: When Jesus finishes speaking about the bread from heaven, many of his disciples say that the saying is hard and walk away. He turns to the Twelve and asks: will you also go away? Peter answers for them all with a question of his own: Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life. He does not say he understands. He says that he knows who has the words. The Catechism teaches that faith is an entirely free gift of God that must be nourished with the word of God and rooted in the faith of the Church. In the Easter season, when the evidence is the empty tomb and a hard saying, that is where faith lives.

scripture.text: Then Jesus said to the twelve: Will you also go away? And Simon Peter answered him: Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

levels.title: The Good Shepherd
levels.reflection: On the fourth Sunday of Easter the Church stops at a field and a flock. I am the good shepherd, says Jesus. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep. I know mine, and mine know me, as the Father knoweth me and I know the Father. The risen Christ is the Shepherd who laid down his life and took it up again. The Catechism teaches that the Church is a sheepfold, the sole and necessary gateway to which is Christ, and a flock that is unfailingly nourished and led by Christ himself, the Good Shepherd and Prince of Shepherds. We are known by name, and led.

scripture.text: I am the good shepherd; and I know mine, and mine know me. As the Father knoweth me, and I know the Father: and I lay down my life for my sheep.

levels.title: I Am the Door
levels.reflection: Jesus speaks of himself as the door of the sheepfold: by me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and he shall go in, and go out, and shall find pastures. There is no other way into the fold and no one is kept out who comes by him. The Church in Acts is learning how wide that door is. When Peter tells the community in Jerusalem what God had done at the house of Cornelius, they hold their peace and glorify God: God then hath also to the Gentiles given repentance unto life. The Catechism says that believing in Jesus Christ and in the One who sent him is necessary for obtaining salvation. The door is a person, and it is open.

scripture.text: I am the door. By me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved: and he shall go in, and go out, and shall find pastures.

levels.title: My Sheep Hear My Voice
levels.reflection: At the feast of the Dedication in Jerusalem, Jesus walks in the porch of Solomon, and the Jews gather round him and ask him to tell them plainly if he is the Christ. He answers that he has told them, but they do not believe because they are not of his sheep. My sheep hear my voice, he says, and I know them, and they follow me. And I give them life everlasting; and they shall not perish for ever, and no man shall pluck them out of my hand. At Antioch the disciples are first named Christians. The Catechism quotes Pope Leo: Christian, recognize your dignity. The name is a gift, and the Shepherd holds those who bear it.

scripture.text: My sheep hear my voice: and I know them, and they follow me. And I give them life everlasting; and they shall not perish for ever, and no man shall pluck them out of my hand.

saint.name: St. Leo the Great
saint.reference: Sermon 22 on the Nativity, 3, as quoted in CCC 1691
saint.text: Christian, recognize your dignity and, now that you share in God's own nature, do not return to your former base condition by sinning. Remember who is your head and of whose body you are a member. Never forget that you have been rescued from the power of darkness and brought into the light of the Kingdom of God.

levels.title: A Light into the World
levels.reflection: Near the end of his public teaching Jesus cries out to the crowd: I am come a light into the world; that whosoever believeth in me may not remain in darkness. If any man hears my words and keeps them not, I do not judge him, for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. The Church has seen in this the whole of her mission. In Antioch the community is ministering to the Lord and fasting when the Holy Spirit says: separate me Saul and Barnabas. Then, fasting and praying, they impose hands and send them away. The Catechism says that the Church has no other light than Christ's, like the moon reflecting the sun.

scripture.text: I am come a light into the world; that whosoever believeth in me, may not remain in darkness. And if any man hear my words, and keep them not, I do not judge him: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.

levels.title: Not Greater Than His Lord
levels.reflection: At the Last Supper, after washing his disciples' feet, Jesus tells them: the servant is not greater than his lord, neither is the apostle greater than he that sent him. Then, in the days after Easter, the apostles live this out. In the synagogue at Antioch in Pisidia, Paul, whom the Church sent out, tells the story of Israel from the exodus to David and shows that God has now fulfilled the promise made to the fathers by raising Jesus. The Catechism says that ecclesial ministry has the character of service, and that those who hold it are slaves of Christ. After Easter the leaders of the Church do not rule from the throne but from the towel.

scripture.text: Amen, amen I say to you: The servant is not greater than his lord; neither is the apostle greater than he that sent him.

levels.title: The Way, the Truth, the Life
levels.reflection: Thomas asks the question every disciple eventually asks: Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way? Jesus answers with a sentence the Church has repeated more than almost any other: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me. The way is not a road. It is a person. In the synagogue at Antioch Paul preaches that the promise made to the fathers has been fulfilled by the raising of Jesus. The Catechism says that in Jesus Christ the whole of God's truth has been made manifest, and that he is the Truth. To follow him is to be going home.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to him: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me.

levels.title: He That Seeth Me
levels.reflection: Philip asks the question we all have: Lord, shew us the Father, and it is enough for us. Jesus answers with surprise and tenderness: have I been so long a time with you, and have you not known me? Philip, he that seeth me seeth the Father also. Then he promises something even more daring: he that believeth in me, the works that I do, he also shall do, and greater than these shall he do. The Catechism teaches that Jesus revealed that God is Father in an unheard-of sense, eternally Father in relation to his only Son. At Antioch Paul and Barnabas say the Lord has commanded them to be a light to the Gentiles, for salvation to the utmost part of the earth.

scripture.text: Jesus saith to him: Have I been so long a time with you; and have you not known me? Philip, he that seeth me seeth the Father also. How sayest thou, shew us the Father?

levels.title: A Place Prepared
levels.reflection: In the fifth week of Easter the Church stays in the upper room, with a sentence meant for hearts that were troubled. In my Father's house there are many mansions. If not, I would have told you: I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go, I will come again, and will take you to myself, that where I am, you also may be. The risen Christ has gone ahead, and heaven is no longer a mystery of distance. The Catechism says that to live in heaven is to be with Christ, and that the elect retain, or rather find, their true identity. St. Ambrose puts it simply: where Christ is, there is life.

scripture.text: In my Father's house there are many mansions. If not, I would have told you: because I go to prepare a place for you. And if I shall go, and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and will take you to myself; that where I am, you also may be.

saint.name: St. Ambrose
saint.reference: Commentary on Luke 10, 121, as quoted in CCC 1025
saint.text: For life is to be with Christ; where Christ is, there is life, there is the kingdom.

levels.title: The Paraclete Will Teach You
levels.reflection: In the upper room Jesus promises that he will not leave his friends alone. If any one love me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and will make our abode with him. And he promises a helper: the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring all things to your mind. The Catechism says that Paraclete means literally one called to one's side, and is commonly translated consoler. At Lystra Paul and Barnabas, mistaken for gods, tear their garments and cry out that they too are mortals, preaching the living God.

scripture.text: But the Paraclete, the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring all things to your mind, whatsoever I shall have said to you.

levels.title: My Peace I Give unto You
levels.reflection: On the night before he died, Jesus said: peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you, not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid. The peace of the risen Christ is not the absence of trouble. Paul and Barnabas, returning to the towns where they had been stoned and driven out, confirm the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, for through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God. The Catechism says earthly peace is the image and fruit of the peace of Christ, the Prince of Peace. This is a peace that has passed through the cross.

scripture.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.

levels.title: The True Vine
levels.reflection: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me. I am the vine: you the branches. The Catechism applies the image to the Church, a choice vineyard planted by the heavenly cultivator, in which the true vine is Christ, who gives life and fruitfulness to the branches. In Jerusalem Peter tells the council that by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we believe to be saved. Easter life is not a life apart from Christ. It is a life drawn from him.

scripture.text: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me. I am the vine: you the branches: he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for without me you can do nothing.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: Commentary on the Gospel of John 21, 8, as quoted in CCC 795
saint.text: Let us rejoice then and give thanks that we have become not only Christians, but Christ himself. Do you understand and grasp, brethren, God's grace toward us? Marvel and rejoice: we have become Christ.

levels.title: That Your Joy May Be Filled
levels.reflection: As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you, says Jesus. Abide in my love. If you keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love, as I also have kept my Father's commandments, and do abide in his love. Then he gives the reason for all he has said: that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be filled. The commandments are not a cage but the shape of a love. The Catechism says the fruits of charity are joy, peace and mercy. Easter joy is not a sentiment. It is the result of staying close to the one who is risen.

scripture.text: As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you. Abide in my love. If you keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love; as I also have kept my Father's commandments, and do abide in his love. These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be filled.

levels.title: No Greater Love
levels.reflection: This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends. Jesus says it on the night before he does it. Then he says what the disciples had not dared to hope: I will not now call you servants, for the servant knoweth not what his lord doth, but I have called you friends, because all things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you. The Catechism says Jesus makes charity the new commandment, and that in loving one another the disciples imitate the love of Jesus they themselves receive. At Jerusalem the Church decides in the Spirit what burdens to lay on the Gentiles.

scripture.text: This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

levels.title: Chosen Out of the World
levels.reflection: Jesus warns his friends that following him is not always welcome. If the world hate you, know ye that it hath hated me before you. If you had been of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. This is not a threat but a preparation. In Acts, Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia beseeching him: pass over into Macedonia, and help us. The Catechism teaches that the disciple of Christ must not only keep the faith but profess it and bear witness to it, amid the persecutions which the Church never lacks. Easter gives courage for exactly that.

scripture.text: If the world hate you, know ye, that it hath hated me before you. If you had been of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.

levels.title: God Is Charity
levels.reflection: In the sixth week of Easter the Church hears the beloved disciple's letter: he that loveth not, knoweth not God: for God is charity. In this is charity: not as though we had loved God, but because he hath first loved us, and sent his Son to be a propitiation for our sins. All that Easter has shown us is an answer to a question God asked first. The Catechism teaches that God's very being is love, an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and that he has destined us to share in that exchange. St. Therese of Lisieux discovered that love was the heart of the Church, the motive force of all the members. Love is where Easter leads.

scripture.text: He that loveth not, knoweth not God: for God is charity.

saint.name: St. Therese of Lisieux
saint.reference: Story of a Soul, as quoted in CCC 826
saint.text: If the Church was a body composed of different members, it couldn't lack the noblest of all; it must have a Heart, and a Heart BURNING WITH LOVE.

levels.title: The Spirit of Truth
levels.reflection: When the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father, says Jesus, the Spirit of truth who proceedeth from the Father, he shall give testimony of me. And you shall give testimony, because you are with me from the beginning. The Spirit does not replace the witness of the apostles. He makes it possible. Paul and Silas, praying and singing in the prison at midnight, show the same thing: a witness who is not afraid. The Catechism says that Jesus promises the Spirit only when the hour has come for his glorification, since his Death and Resurrection will fulfill the promise made to the fathers. Easter and the Spirit belong together.

scripture.text: But when the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceedeth from the Father, he shall give testimony of me. And you shall give testimony, because you are with me from the beginning.

saint.name: St. Basil the Great
saint.reference: On the Holy Spirit 15, 36, as quoted in CCC 736
saint.text: Through the Holy Spirit we are restored to paradise, led back to the Kingdom of heaven, and adopted as children, given confidence to call God "Father" and to share in Christ's grace, called children of light and given a share in eternal glory.

levels.title: It Is Expedient That I Go
levels.reflection: Jesus tells the disciples something that sounds like a loss: it is expedient to you that I go, for if I go not, the Paraclete will not come to you, but if I go, I will send him to you. They are sad because they do not yet see what he will become to them. The Catechism says that the Spirit of truth will be given in answer to Jesus' prayer and will teach us everything, remind us of what Christ said, and bear witness to him. In Athens Paul stands in the Areopagus and finds an altar to the unknown God, and tells his hearers: what you worship without knowing it, that I preach to you. Christ goes so that we may know him wherever we are.

scripture.text: But I tell you the truth: it is expedient to you that I go: for if I go not, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.

levels.title: All Truth
levels.reflection: When he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth. For he shall not speak of himself; but what things soever he shall hear, he shall speak; and the things that are to come, he shall shew you. The Spirit is not a rival voice to Christ. He is the breath of the Word, carrying the same truth into every age. In Corinth the Lord tells Paul in the night: do not fear, but speak; and hold not thy peace, because I am with thee. The Catechism teaches that the Spirit, since Easter, leads the disciples into all the truth. Fear gives way to witness.

scripture.text: But when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth. For he shall not speak of himself; but what things soever he shall hear, he shall speak; and the things that are to come, he shall shew you.

saint.name: St. Gregory of Nazianzus
saint.reference: Theological Orations 5, 26, as quoted in CCC 684
saint.text: Now the Spirit dwells among us and grants us a clearer vision of himself.

levels.title: Forty Days
levels.reflection: Luke says that Jesus showed himself alive after his passion by many proofs, for forty days appearing to the apostles and speaking of the kingdom of God. Forty days after Easter the Church keeps the Ascension, on a Thursday, or, where the bishops have moved the feast, on the following Sunday. The Catechism says that during these forty days the risen Lord eats and drinks familiarly with his disciples and teaches them about the kingdom, but his glory remains veiled, and that the Ascension marks the transition from the glory of the risen Christ to that of Christ exalted at the Father's right hand. The forty days are a school for the Church. The next days are the waiting.

scripture.text: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion, by many proofs, for forty days appearing to them, and speaking of the kingdom of God.

levels.title: Sorrow into Joy
levels.reflection: Jesus tells his friends what the days ahead will be: you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice; and you shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. Not replaced by joy. Turned into joy, as the cross became Easter. I will see you again, he says, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man shall take from you. The Catechism says Jesus Christ precedes us into the Father's kingdom so that we, the members of his Body, may live in the hope of one day being with him for ever. The apostles will have to learn to hold both the absence and the promise, and so do we. Apollos, in Ephesus, is taught the way of the Lord more fully by Priscilla and Aquila.

scripture.text: Amen, amen I say to you, that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice; and you shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

levels.title: Ask in My Name
levels.reflection: In that day you shall not ask me any thing, says Jesus. Amen, amen I say to you: if you ask the Father any thing in my name, he will give it you. Hitherto you have not asked any thing in my name. Ask, and you shall receive; that your joy may be full. The Catechism says that what is new in the prayer Jesus taught is to ask in his name, and that faith in the Son introduces the disciples into the knowledge of the Father. We pray to the Father through Christ who has gone before us and who lives to make intercession. Easter is a school of prayer. St. John Chrysostom reminds us that prayer is possible while walking in public, buying or selling, or even cooking.

scripture.text: And in that day you shall not ask me any thing. Amen, amen I say to you: if you ask the Father any thing in my name, he will give it you. Hitherto you have not asked any thing in my name. Ask, and you shall receive; that your joy may be full.

saint.name: St. John Chrysostom
saint.reference: Ecloga on Prayer 2, as quoted in CCC 2743
saint.text: It is possible to offer fervent prayer even while walking in public or strolling alone, or seated in your shop, . . . while buying or selling, . . . or even while cooking.

levels.title: Why Stand You Looking Up?
levels.reflection: He led them out as far as Bethania, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them, and whilst he blessed them, he departed from them and was carried up to heaven. A cloud received him out of their sight. Two men in white ask the apostles a question the Church still hears: ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven. Before leaving, Jesus told them: you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit, and you shall be witnesses unto me even to the uttermost part of the earth. The Catechism says that being seated at the Father's right hand signifies the inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom. He has not left us. He has gone ahead.

scripture.text: Who also said: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

levels.title: I Have Overcome the World
levels.reflection: At the end of the Last Supper Jesus gathers up everything he has said: these things I have spoken to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you shall have distress: but have confidence, I have overcome the world. In Ephesus Paul meets disciples who had been baptized with the baptism of John, and asks: have you received the Holy Spirit since ye believed? They have not so much as heard of him. They are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, Paul lays his hands on them, and the Holy Spirit comes upon them. The Catechism says that from that time on the apostles imparted to the newly baptized, by the laying on of hands, the gift of the Spirit that completes the grace of Baptism.

scripture.text: These things I have spoken to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you shall have distress: but have confidence, I have overcome the world.

levels.title: This Is Eternal Life
levels.reflection: In his prayer to the Father on the night before he died, Jesus says what eternal life is: that they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent. It is not first a place or a length of days. It is knowing. The Catechism says God put us in the world to know, to love and to serve him, and so to come to paradise. In his farewell to the elders of Ephesus Paul says: I fear none of these things, neither do I count my life more precious than myself, so that I may consummate my course and the ministry of the word. Knowing God shapes a whole life, and a whole life is a way of knowing him.

scripture.text: Now this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.

levels.title: Thy Word Is Truth
levels.reflection: Jesus prays to the Father for his disciples: sanctify them in truth. Thy word is truth. He asks that they be made holy by the truth and not by any human cleverness. In Miletus Paul tells the elders of Ephesus how to do their work: support the weak, and remember the word of the Lord Jesus, how he said: it is a more blessed thing to give, rather than to receive. The Catechism says that love for the poor is incompatible with immoderate love of riches or their selfish use. The truth that sanctifies is the same truth that opens the hand. Holiness in the apostolic Church had a particular shape: it was truthful, and it was generous.

scripture.text: Sanctify them in truth. Thy word is truth.

levels.title: That They All May Be One
levels.reflection: In the last part of his prayer Jesus prays for those who will believe through the apostles' word: that they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee; that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. The unity of Christians is part of the witness of the Gospel. The Catechism says Christ always gives his Church the gift of unity, but that the Church must always pray and work to maintain, reinforce and perfect the unity Christ wills for her. At Jerusalem the Lord stands by Paul in the night and tells him: be constant; for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome. Unity and witness go together.

scripture.text: That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee; that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.

levels.title: Feed My Sheep
levels.reflection: After the breakfast by the lake, Jesus turns to Peter: Simon son of John, lovest thou me more than these? Peter says: yea, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee. Feed my lambs. Three times he asks, three times Peter answers, until Peter is grieved, and says: Lord, thou knowest all things. Feed my sheep. The three questions answer the three denials. The Catechism says the Lord made Simon alone the rock of his Church, gave him the keys, and instituted him shepherd of the whole flock, and that this pastoral office belongs to the Church's foundation and is continued by the bishops under the primacy of the Pope. Mercy restores, and then it sends.

scripture.text: When therefore they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter: Simon son of John, lovest thou me more than these? He saith to him: Yea, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee. He saith to him: Feed my lambs.

levels.title: Without Prohibition
levels.reflection: John closes his Gospel with a sigh of wonder: there are also many other things which Jesus did; which, if they were written every one, the world itself, I think, would not be able to contain the books that should be written. The story of Easter is not finished by any book. Luke closes Acts on a note of calm certainty. Paul remains two whole years in his own hired lodging at Rome, receiving all who come to him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ with all confidence, without prohibition. The Catechism says all Christians have an obligation to manifest the new man they put on in Baptism and to reveal the power of the Holy Spirit by whom they were strengthened at Confirmation. Tomorrow the Spirit comes.

scripture.text: And he remained two whole years in his own hired lodging; and he received all that came in to him, Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, without prohibition.

levels.title: Filled with the Holy Spirit
levels.reflection: On the fiftieth day, when the days of the Pentecost were accomplished, they were all together in one place. Suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a mighty wind, and it filled the whole house. There appeared to them parted tongues as it were of fire, and it sat upon every one of them. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with divers tongues. The Catechism says that on this day Christ's Passover is fulfilled in the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and that the Church was made manifest to the world. Fire symbolizes the transforming energy of the Spirit's actions. Easter ends where the Church begins: the risen Lord has given his Spirit, and the Church goes out.

scripture.text: And when the days of the Pentecost were accomplished, they were all together in one place: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a mighty wind coming, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. And there appeared to them parted tongues as it were of fire, and it sat upon every one of them: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they began to speak with divers tongues, according as the Holy Ghost gave them to speak.

saint.name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
saint.reference: Commentary on John 11, 11, as quoted in CCC 738
saint.text: All of us who have received one and the same Spirit, that is, the Holy Spirit, are in a sense blended together with one another and with God. For if Christ, together with the Father's and his own Spirit, comes to dwell in each of us, though we are many, still the Spirit is one and undivided. He binds together the spirits of each and every one of us, . . . and makes all appear as one in him.

The apostolic faith

He opened the gates of paradise

So that the Law might be abolished
So that the temple might be rebuilt

The wisdom of the elders

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to ____ the things that are God's."

Five barley loaves and two fishes
Two loaves and five fishes

questions.prompt: What does Jesus tell his disciples to do when all are filled, in John 6:12?

Share the rest with the poor of the city
Bring the remains into the temple
Gather up the fragments that remain, lest they be lost

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say to the frightened disciples in John 6:20?

Peace be to you; fear not

Twelve men from each of the tribes of Israel

Five teachers from the synagogues

questions.prompt: Where does Jesus say, in Luke 24:44, that all things must needs be fulfilled which are written concerning him?

In the writings of the elders and the traditions
In the book of the covenant and the tables of stone

questions.explanation: Jesus says: "all things must needs be fulfilled, which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me."

Only one single Word

Three Words, one for each person

A multitude of angels around the throne
The temple filled with smoke
A great light and a voice from the cloud

questions.prompt: What will the Paraclete do, according to John 14:26?

Comfort the sorrowful in their afflictions
Lead you into the land of promise
Judge the world in righteousness

questions.explanation: Jesus says: "the Paraclete, the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring all things to your mind, whatsoever I shall have said to you."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Paraclete literally means he who is called to one's side.
questions.explanation: Catechism 692 says Jesus calls the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, "literally, 'he who is called to one's side.'"

questions.prompt: What do Paul and Barnabas say to the crowd who think they are gods, according to Acts 14:14?
choices: We are the sons of the prophets
We also are mortals, men like unto you
We are the servants of the Most High
We are the messengers of the temple

questions.explanation: Paul and Barnabas cried: "We also are mortals, men like unto you, preaching to you to be converted from these vain things, to the living God."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say in John 14:27 about the peace he gives?
choices: Not as the world giveth, do I give unto you
Even as the dew falleth, so I give to you
As the Father gave to Moses, so I give to you
As the angels gave at my birth, so I give
questions.correctAnswer: Not as the world giveth, do I give unto you
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "Let not your ____ be troubled, nor let it be afraid."
questions.explanation: John 14:27 ends: "Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid."

questions.prompt: What do Paul and Barnabas tell the disciples, in Acts 14:21?
choices: The kingdom is at hand, and repentance is near
Through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God
The Lord will deliver you from all affliction
Give no occasion to your enemies and be at peace
questions.correctAnswer: Through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is earthly peace the image and fruit of?
choices: The wisdom of rulers
The peace of Christ
The order of creation
The unity of the nations
questions.explanation: Catechism 2305 says: "Earthly peace is the image and fruit of the peace of Christ, the messianic 'Prince of Peace.'"

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "I am the true vine; and my Father is the ____."
questions.explanation: John 15:1 reads: "I am the true vine; and my Father is the husbandman."

questions.prompt: According to John 15:5, what can the branches do without the vine?
choices: Little
Much
Nothing
Something
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "he that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for without me you can do nothing."

questions.prompt: According to Acts 15:11, by what do Peter and the Church believe they are saved?
choices: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ
The blood of the covenant of Abraham
The works of the Law of Moses
The prayers of the elders
questions.correctAnswer: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Peter says: "by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, we believe to be saved, in like manner as they also."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the true vine is Christ, who gives life and fruitfulness to the branches.
questions.explanation: Catechism 755 says: "the true vine is Christ who gives life and fruitfulness to the branches, that is, to us, who through the Church remain in Christ, without whom we can do nothing."

questions.prompt: According to John 15:9, how has the Father loved Jesus?
choices: As Jesus has loved his disciples
As he loved Israel in the desert
As he loved the angels of heaven
As he loved Abraham and the fathers
questions.correctAnswer: As Jesus has loved his disciples
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you. Abide in my love."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say will happen if his disciples keep his commandments, in John 15:10?
choices: They shall be filled with the Spirit
They shall abide in his love
They shall be called friends of God
They shall see the Father
questions.correctAnswer: They shall abide in his love
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "If you keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be ____."
questions.explanation: John 15:11 ends: "that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be filled."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what are the fruits of charity?
choices: Joy, peace, and mercy
Wisdom, counsel, and fortitude
Prayer, fasting, and almsgiving
Faith, hope, and love
questions.explanation: Catechism 1829 says: "The fruits of charity are joy, peace, and mercy."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say is his commandment, in John 15:12?
choices: That you serve one another, as I have served you
That you forgive one another, as I have forgiven you
That you keep the sabbath, as I have kept it
That you love one another, as I have loved you

questions.explanation: Jesus says: "This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you."

questions.prompt: Jesus says: "I have called you ____: because all things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you."
questions.explanation: John 15:15 reads: "But I have called you friends: because all things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you."

questions.prompt: What does the council of Jerusalem say in Acts 15:28?
choices: It hath seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to us, to lay no further burden upon you
It is needful that every convert be circumcised
It is the will of the apostles that the Law of Moses be kept
It is written that the Gentiles shall be as the sons of Israel

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Jesus makes the Law of Moses the new commandment.

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say in John 15:18 about the world's hatred?
choices: It cannot touch the soul of the faithful
It hath hated me before you
It is the fault of the disciples
It shall pass when the Lord returns
questions.correctAnswer: It hath hated me before you
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "If the world hate you, know ye, that it hath hated me before you."

questions.prompt: Why does Jesus say the world hateth his disciples, in John 15:19?
choices: Because he has chosen them out of the world
Because they have left the temple
Because they have kept the Law of Moses
Because they have broken the customs of the fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Because he has chosen them out of the world
questions.explanation: Jesus says: "because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you."

questions.prompt: What did the man of Macedonia say to Paul in the vision, in Acts 16:9?
choices: Come to Rome, and testify of the Lord
Build up the churches that thou hast planted
Go not into Asia, for the Lord forbids it
Pass over into Macedonia, and help us

questions.explanation: Luke writes: "a vision was shewed to Paul in the night, which was a man of Macedonia standing and beseeching him, and saying: Pass over into Macedonia, and help us."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the disciple of Christ must not only keep the faith but also profess it and bear witness to it.
questions.explanation: Catechism 1816 says: "The disciple of Christ must not only keep the faith and live on it, but also profess it, confidently bear witness to it, and spread it."

questions.prompt: St. John writes: "He that loveth not, knoweth not God: for God is ____."
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:8 reads: "He that loveth not, knoweth not God: for God is charity."

questions.prompt: According to 1 John 4:10, who loved first?

God, who hath first loved us
The Church, which was gathered
The prophets, who loved the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: God, who hath first loved us
questions.explanation: St. John writes: "In this is charity: not as though we had loved God, but because he hath first loved us."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, God himself is an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
questions.explanation: Catechism 221 says: "God himself is an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and he has destined us to share in that exchange."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does it say God's very being is?
choices: Power
Light
Love
Wisdom
questions.explanation: Catechism 221 says that St. John affirms that "God is love": "God's very being is love."

questions.prompt: According to John 15:26, who proceedeth from the Father and shall give testimony of Jesus?

The Spirit of truth
The angel of the Lord
The Baptist

questions.prompt: What did Paul and Silas do at midnight in the prison at Philippi, according to Acts 16:25?

They fasted and wept
They called out for the jailer
They preached to the other prisoners

questions.prompt: What does the jailer ask, and how do they answer, in Acts 16:30-31?

Why were you set free? The angel opened the doors
questions.correctAnswer: What must I do to be saved? Believe in the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved
questions.explanation: The jailer said: "Masters, what must I do, that I may be saved?" They said: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house."

questions.prompt: What does Jesus say in John 16:7 is expedient to the disciples?
choices: That he abide
That he be silent
That he go
That he teach again

A list of the offerings to Zeus
A statue of the goddess of wisdom
An image of the god of the sea

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Jesus promises the Holy Spirit from the first day of his public life.

questions.prompt: What does the Lord say to Paul at Corinth, in Acts 18:9?

questions.explanation: The Lord said to Paul in the night: "Do not fear, but speak; and hold not thy peace, Because I am with thee."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the Holy Spirit teaches the disciples and guides them into all the truth.

Forty days

The fall of Jerusalem
The works of the Law
The kingdom of God

His freedom

His life
